name: Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous - Enhanced Edition

data: Amazing game, amazing story, I love this game so much,
Great story (so far) and excellent game mechanics
I love the replayability of this game and the story is amazing
It is very challenging and i love it
Combat feels great, characters are amazing, story is really good, and I personally really like the love this game receives through mods and community
the writing is just so, SO boring
the MANY bugs and terrible balance were too much that I just uninstalled
the actual gameplay is just so boring and tedious to me
Game difficulty pacing is poor, combat is bland, overly complex ruleset, bad AI, forgettable plot
So it's a not recommend until they patch it
the character creation is just way too much
That's a shame because the writing is good
it ends in boring silly story and annoying additional army mechanics
Too many unfixed bugs, and the settlement/commander stuff ruins the game
Consistent bugs in the vanilla game, unmodded, are just too rampant
-Are long identified bugs ignored and now baked in forever as jank
Can't recommend that one because the gameplay is trash:
they made combat such a slog that it's unfun
Combat was repetitive and extremly unbalanced
And the actual gameplay is a curse on normal and I felt no shame about bumping the difficulty way, way down
If you want the actual printed stats for enemies as written, that is at the Core difficulty setting
Some puzzles are too hard to understand what you're supposed to see in order to solve
it all is worthless because you have to play the way the devs want you to and the classes they want
And devs dont bothers to fix anything, so wheres expect fun build you get just dissapointment instead
the devs decided instead of making the game tactical that you would be required to have a math degree

Pretty great CPRG, however it is a very big game. Combat gets kinda boring late-gam but thankfully you can adjust difficulty.

Pathfinder world/setting is pretty interesting, and the story/characters are good. Combat can feel a bit overwhelming if coming from simpler crpgs. 
Really good story reactivity and replay value, but the replay value goes down when you realize it's a 150 hour game. 
Some quests have some poorly designed puzzles that might require guides or lots of guesswork. Otherwise, it's up there with Baldur's Gate 3/ Baldur's Gate 2
Solid 9/10 game
Great game. High initial learning curve, but worth it with all the different ways to play and replay the game

nice turn-based rpg. Only complaint is that, unlike D&D online there is a stiff charge of in-game currency to create new characters. Trying out different class combinations & then taking the character for a spin was one of my favorite parts of that game. Here you would have to start many games (and go through the leveling-up process & storyline breaks) to do the same.
I really liked both Kingmaker and This game. I wish they had more Pathfinder on the horizon. I'd love to 4-6 Pathfinder 1e Adventure Paths made into games.
i was looking for something as mesmerizing as BG3 and here i found a game that engaged me even more. Maybe technologically not as advanced but the story and well written characters make up for it.

This is like Kingmaker but -slightly- less austere and WAY harder.

Well I guess it really is harder because unlike Kingmaker I didn't look up any guides for my main character and tried to play a devil summoner build lel my bad,

Anyway 212h playthrough on hard difficulty, if you like old school CRPGs and don't pay too much attention to graphics you'll get your money's worth.

I've played through 600+ hours of this already jesus. Had a healthy dose of masochism at the start given how many bugs were still in the game when i started playing, but it definitely improved. A must-play if you were/are into oldschool isometric rpg's.

I want to recommend this game but I really can't. There are several game breaking bugs, including one where a banner (mechanic than influences morale and recruitment) just goes red, and you have no way of fixing it while everything goes negative. 20 hour playthrough down the drain and I'm lucky I caught it early. Don't buy this game til it has a few bug fix patches. I'm tabling it til there's a patch.

Edit: they've patched a few bugs, I ended up putting crusade mode on auto. Still don't recommend this til a few more months and patches have passed

As others have mentioned, this game is essentially just spyware with an invasive EULA and tracking of PC activities. I let the game sit at the EULA's "I decline" page for 2 hours just so I could leave this review. I'm unfortunately unable to refund as I bought this during a prior Steam Sale. Would not recommend (at least not without locking down the game somehow using a VPN or firewall, etc.).

Like the first game. Difficult to get in to and even harder to master but a great CRPG for those that give it the time it needs.
Great and interesting Companions, Nigh infinite builds which only forces you to meta game on hardest difficulties and a story where you decide who you wan't to be, well worth the price.

The dlc's are not required, they are mostly a bonus for those that really like the gameplay and are good for experimenting with builds and for more content to try them out in.
Fun. Another turn-based D&D like RPG. Pathfinderr rules, but plays a bit like Balders Gate 3 or Solasta. I enjoyed it

A _significant_ improvement over the first game. They managed to improve on almost every facet of the game: art design, UI, narrative, agency - if you liked Kingmaker, this one will has everything the first one had and more.

Unfortunately, the "crusade minigame" is as problematic as the "kingdom management" of Kingmaker, and there's still more bugs and interface problems than I'm confortable with. There's certainly room for improvement in future patches/games.

That being said, if you're a fan of Pathfinder or good CRPGs, _Wrath of the Righteous_ is a must play. Congratulations to Owlcat on the great improvements made!

82 hours in, working on Act 3, and I'm feeling like I'm just starting to come to grips with the game and its mechanics. It's got a complicated learning curver, but the story and game play are really good. A warning that this game may not be for everyone, even those who likes CRPGs.

Added after initial review:
I got into act 4 and the game changes at that point, and not really for the better. The map turns into this one large area with smaller sub areas, and it became difficult to determine exactly what to do to move the story forward, which is disappointing. I still love the game, but going into act 4 kind wrecked my playthrough.

urgh, ive given up on this game for now. Not enjoying the combat. Its hard to learn the combat when you are forced into a 2 hours fighting senario where waves and waves of enemies attacked my base and I couldn't save the game at any point and so manage to failed right at the end when the NPC defenders just stood around doing almost nothing.

Ive gone to do a few other fights and accept this loss but my group just isnt great and I'm too newbie to boot. My rogue I created for my main character is rubbish compared to the one that joined me, I cant kick myself obvs. My ranger guy is good, but my mage and melee druid dude cant hit anything for toffee and are taking up valuable space. I havent had enough time in the game to gear up in any meaningful way, my characters havent been able to collect any good weapons, and combat is really boring miss miss miss miss miss miss. very frustrating. I hope to come back at some stage, but having played Planetscape, BG2, Divinity 2, Icewind Dale etc, I just cant get into this one.

I want to come back, but ive given it 20 hours, and hardly done much.

This game should be named Wrath of the Reloading! I have over 500+ hours due to reloading and having to replay.

Can't exit a building due to no exit icon to click? RELOAD!
Quest item not where it's supposed to be? RELOAD!
Companion disappear mid quest to never be seen again? RELOAD!
Your pet not following you or not appearing when you enter/exit new area? RELOAD!
Achievement not counted after you fulfill the requirements? RELOAD!
Made a mistake respecing? RELOAD!
Screen all black after entering new map? RELOAD?!? Nope got to restart entire game!

Dev's response: Just keep reloading old saves. Literally it in was their last patch fix notes. Not that they fixed companion issues, but to just lose your progress and keep reloading...

Owlcat keep pumping out the DLC you can overcharge for instead of fixing current issues!

Incredibly complex, vast and detailled CRPG, to the point of being a little overwhelming at times. The story kept me going through the more sluggish parts though. Thoroughly, enjoyed my playthrough even though it feels like you would need to play it 10 times to see everything.

I picked up this game in a Humble Bundle, and fired it up on a whim, as it seemed like a fun little diversion for a week or so.

Heh. Yeaaaah... Don't let that 'Time played at time of review" overwhelm you too much. I restarted about 50 hours in with a walkthrough when I realized how much of the game I'd inadvertently missed, and that total also includes all of the playable DLC.

Totally worth it.

If you want a 200+ hour monster of a table-top campaign-turned-CRPG to sink your teeth into, stop reading and buy.

Now.

Even if it's at full price. Honestly, maybe even especially if it's at full price. It's worth it.

Very nice character creation, and 1e systems feel at least learnably intuitive. Maybe a little rough compared to 2e, maybe less balanced in some places, but very much a great time if you like the Pathfinder 1e system.

The best CRPG of all time. So many choices, so many good companions (except you Daeren and Woljif), and a priceless journey across the land. The freedom in mythic paths and build choices is just unprecedented here.

This is a deep and crunchy RPG with so many options that it can melt your brain if you look at it for to long. Owlcat heard the challenge to adapt pathfinder one and said "bet".

10/10, Even better then BG3.

Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous is an impressive CRPG with a deep, engaging story and a richly detailed world. Its branching paths and meaningful choices make every playthrough unique and immersive. 
The game offers a rewarding challenge, though the mechanics can feel overwhelming for those unfamiliar with Pathfinder rules (I'd prefer DND 5e).

Damn If Owlcat had more budged for pathfinder series they could do much much more. I really liked companions in this game but one. I think 90% of them were well written, their quest chains were well done. Overall this is very well made crpg.

All in all this is a good game. It suffers from inconsistent writing quality - some parts are very good and others are poorly written, childish and pretty silly. Saying that, its a fun game that offers a huge amount of content- it take weeks or even months to finish, most of which is fun. 

If you like Kingmaker, than this game would be a good followup.

Enjoyed playing this game. Great story, interesting characters. Tough to learn the action economy for individuals that haven't played the Pathfinder TTRPG but over all a quality play. Very crunchy character building if you are into that.
There are endless possibilities to this game, if you're a fan of CRPG's I recommend it for sure. Can be overwhelming when you first start but it unfolds as you go on.
Bad game design, do not recommend. Play the divinity games and Baldurs Gate 3 instead.

The game is downright incredible, both in terms of quality and value for money. The character customization is quite good, and matches Pathfinder 1e pretty well. Extremely fun, story's pretty good, and the characters are distinctive and mostly memorable. It is quite difficult on Core and above, at which point you actually have to know what you're doing. Bring dispel magic.

Highly recommend, 10/10

Baldur's gate 3 reignited my love for the RPG genre after growing up with games such as BG2 and the Icewind Dale series. What BG3 has in production quality this game has in sheer scope. It's just as good as BG3 but with other strengths. Pathfinder:WoTR recreates the old BG2 type of RPG perfectly.

170h for one playthrough in this classic, table-top inspired, RPG. There is a lot to do and try out. Certain elements feel like a drag, cringe or breaking the immersion, but the game still delivers. The UI/UX needs more attention.

Far superior than Kingmaker, Wrath of the Righteous was great. I did the Azata path which is one of the best, most touching and epic gaming moments ive ever had, i wont say more because of spoilers. Amazing story, characters & companions, music and sidequests and many different endings and outcomes. There are some issues in difficulty balancing but with a few tweaks in options and after you get the hang of it, things will be OK, but keep in mind the game is very challenging in a lot of battles, you need to be very thoughtful in the builds you create and the party disposition. Also the crusade mode was a bit lackluster. Besides these things, the game was very very good in all other aspects. Must have and must play for any RPG and TTRPG fan.
This is not a starter RPG, this is advanced RPG. A lot to take in and pretty complicated to start out but I'm having a lot of fun. 100 hours in as of now and I'm not even sure I'm halfway

I'm a really big fan of turn based rpg games. Starting from fallout 1&2, ending up with divinity as one of the best games of the genre. I wanted something to give me a similar kick. I wanted this 3d camera change divinity (& wasteland) had, turn based, rich story.

Boy, did that have it all! It feels more deep and complete, close to tabletop d&d. Rich story, long campaign, choices, classes.

Just perfect. Keep up the good work!!

Buggy, poorly voice acted, poorly written, obnoxious choices.

Multiple quests will fail with no warning (Explore the Murky Grotto, for instance) and there will come times when you lose crusade morale because the game is hard locked into certain milestones. UI is atrocious and routinely forgets to inform you when enemy armies are attacking or when quest steps are available.

A poor Baldur's Gate wannabe clone.

The crusade mode is the most joykilling slog of useless $#!$!% I've ever seen in a game like this and it drains every ounce of enjoyment from whatever the overly-cartoonish (the art style is obnoxious) remainder of the game which drowns in repetitiveness quickly. I've tried enjoying this game on multiple starts stacking up significant hours. I breakdown halfway through, always. Once you have to start doing major things in crusade mode, the game just dies.

What should have been a great experience is marred by some truly dreadful balancing. The game swings wildly from a walk in the park, to massive difficulty with no rhyme or reason.
The game balance assumes you are constantly save scumming so that you can buff up before non-trivial fights.

It also has the worst puzzles I've experienced in any game.

I stuck with the game far longer than I should have, getting about halfway through before the balancing finally made me uninstall it. What finally pushed me over the edge was yet another untelegraphed major encounter, where the boss could hit any member of my party on a roll of 2 (thanks to having +51 to hit) while most of my characters would only hit it on a 20.

Good game :), I been looking for something post Bladurs gate. Of course this game is not a DnD adventure as the game has rails in terms of dialog and stories, nevertheless I think this game is the best approach to a DnD with a fixed story even better in some aspects to Baldurs Gate. got it on offer for like 5 dls and it was a steal will be looking for season pass offers and continue to support the developer

This is actually a fantastic game. It takes a while to really get used to the system and the skill cap is actually very high. The game really doesn't help you out much though, if you are new to literally Owlcat Games Pathfinder, just play on lower difficulties. Even on normal you will find yourself frustrated. Only after ~200 hours do I feel confident enough to play on Core difficulty.

But a true gem here.

Where should one begin....The overwhelming flavour of old school role playing is thick in the air..Character creation is "full"in its most elongated and comprehensive manifestation of just how it should be.So many rpg"s fall woefully short when offering the player their input and aspiration for their character.But once done,,...we enter a world new yet familiar...This game is just RIGHT..I believe this is the true successor to Baldurs Gate 1&2
and the people behind this franchise should stay the course because they are quite justifiably on to a winner.There is nothing this good on any far horizon....This is role playing,..nothing more and nothing less

Excelent game, better than the D&D series games put together. This is a way better baldur's gate with a much better story and characters. The game has it's woke moments but the characters are done so well that it "works", I'm not annoyed by it for the most part so far.
More voiceacting would also help a lot, maybe this will get expanded upon in future updates. Story, characters, options, gameplay, graphics, voiceacting, all great. Core difficulty level is tough, be prepared to save and replay some encounters a lot and use everything that gives you an advantage or choose a lower difficulty level. Props to the devs, this is worth your money.

TONS, I repeat, TONS of character choices during creation and after. Great writing. Companions you'll love and some you'll hate. You won't get penalized for leaving those companions out or even killing them should the opportunity arise. My only CON for the game would be crusader mode. I'd prefer to focus solely on the party and the story, To be fair they do have an option for you to turn Crusader Mode off but you will lose out on certain benefits and even some mythic path options which makes it a very difficult decision.

One of the best RPGs imo, I keep thinking about this game fondly months after playing through it. Infinite replayability. Choices actually matter. The characters were also written pretty well. The main story is top tier. 10/10 game.

Best replayable CRPG I've ever played. With its many DLCs and endings, there are many ways to build your character to play this.
I'm nominating this game for 2024's Labor of Love!

Very much improved from Kingmaker, the Pathfinder system allows for plenty of interesting character builds and roleplaying options.
Great writing as usual from Owlcat, make sure to download "Better Buffs" or "Buff it 2 the limit" to remove the single biggest annoyance with the game: prebuffing. Without one of these mods the game is a chore, hope the next comes with this functionality baked in.

Abelard, leave a positive review.

I got on sale not expecting much, I love this game way more than I expected. Be warned, definitely can be confusing (classes, subclasses, etc). Very dnd like, but that also requires players have some familiarity, or that they are willing to take the time to figure it out. There are also ways to be either more or less involved in the specifics of your character's build, but it's hard to play the whole game without any knowledge of how the system works. Also the game can get more tedious in later stages, especially if you're a completionist (which I happen to be a bit of). Regardless, it's still a great game. Offers a ton of freedom in what you can chose to do. I'd recommend to anyone who is interested, likes the genre, and is willing to give the game a chance. I mean the game has a ton of care put into it, even if it feels like a little too much sometimes. Btw Daeran is the best.
This is probably the best RPG I have ever played and I have played a lot. I felt though all my adventures that I was able to do what I wanted and the game would accept it. 10/10 Would recommend!

An epic journey that took forever (300h, completing almost all sidequests (some become unavailable if you choose the opposite questline).
Great story and characters drove me forward the entire time.
Challenging battles for me on normal difficulty - specially in the beginning. Get's easier after 20h.
Once your generals reached a higher level their magic makes also the Heroes-of-Might- and-Magic-like-mini-games-battles a lot easier.
No bugs or crashes.
Didn't want to play it at first when I read that certain quests had time restrictions. But in retrospective there is really more than enough time to complete almost all of them.
9/10.

The game is quite interesting. Came here after the beautiful experience in Baldurs Gate 3.
The game has a lot of things at the same time. This is the big plus, as well as the biggest drawback of the game. Some of the missions and encounters are looking like to be placed just to extend amount of content and say this to gamers - we added 200+ hours of gameplay.
- 1/2 of skills can be removed from the game.
- 1/2 of quests SHOULD have been removed from the game. (starting from act 3)
- 3/4 of battles should have been removed from the game.

I wasn't able to play the game after the middle of the act 3 since most of the battles/quests/decisions/crusade were busted and not interesting at all.
Anyways the game is good and worth a try at lest from the character building aspect.

An unbalanced beautiful catastrophe. You need to be willing to play dirty to win, but this may only apply to the Core difficulties and higher as I haven't played any of the lower difficulties. Only reservation I have is that spell resistance is a bit annoying as a high level spell can be completely negated and high AC makes weapons not as viable.

Baldurs Gate 3 came out about a week ago, but out of respect to this game I refuse to play it until finishing my current playthrough. Great characters, extremely dark and gritty setting... Ran into an underground prison ran by demons, found a giant Minotaur in charge of the prison, I spilled grease on the floor before fighting him, he slipped and spent the entire fight face down on the ground 10/10

damn took me over 200 hours to finish this game in one month and on normal of all things.
i have to say that despite the great story and replay ability this is the most troublesome CRPG i played. it's not always clear what items,skills,spells and feats do. and i had spend hours of youtube learning how to play. it relies on pathfinder rule set is no excuse the game should stand on it's on. so i recommend this game if you have alot of spare time to learn how to play other wise you will struggle more then enjoy.

The best game I've ever played, it's up there with the mass effect trilogy.
+ Beautiful story
+ Interesting and varied companions (Regill and Arueshalae are perfect)
+ Amazing world building
+ 10/10 Soundtrack 
+ combat that genuinely allows you to do everything 
I only hope they'll make another Pathfinder game.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly object to a late EULA change and third-party tracking software that players say cannot be opted out of.
A later official announcement says the tracking software was removed from the game and the EULA was restored to the previous version.

tldr.text: Very Positive (82%): players love the story and characters.
The most common complaint is the writing and characters, with bugs and crashes close behind.

details.text: Recent reviews complain far less about bugs and crashes, at 8% against 18% overall.
Newer players are far less positive than veterans, and those who have played the longest are the most positive group.
